clue.text: Witty person such as joker

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an amusing, eccentric character
second meaning: one of a pack, of which the joker is an example

explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the joker a comedian, echoing the witty person; in the second meaning it is the extra card in a pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a real card is an idiom for an entertaining wag, and a joker is one item from a deck.

clue.text: Headwear measured and turned over

parts.note: a cap is a piece of headwear
sized means measured for size

explanation.surface: A hat is fitted to the head and then flipped upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a milliner's routine; 'turned over' is the boating sense, not a hat being inspected.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that has capsized has rolled upside down in the water, which is what turned over describes.

clue.text: Some future ignoramuses to be in command

indicators.note: 'some' means only a portion, so the answer is a run of letters lying inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A grumble that ignorant people will be ruling us in years to come.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles futuRE IGNoramuses.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who reigns holds sovereign power, so to reign is to rule or hold authority over a country.

clue.text: Supply lid going over cooking vessel

parts.note: a stock is a supply kept in reserve

indicators.note: to go over is to flip, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: a top is a lid

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put a lid over a cooking pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going over' looks like a lid covering the pan, but it turns the lid upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A large deep pan used for simmering bones and vegetables into broth is a kitchen pot, which a vessel is.

clue.text: Container of valuables secure and threats diverted

indicators.note: diverted things are sent off course, so these letters are rerouted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strongbox of valuables is made safe and any threats to it are fended off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secure' reads as an instruction to lock up the box, but it is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate's box of gold and jewels is the classic image, a storage box holding riches.

clue.text: Name of man that's caught nits brought up

parts.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up reads it from the bottom, so it runs backwards

parts.note: nits are lice and their eggs

explanation.surface: A man is identified by having picked up head lice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' suggests raising a subject, but here it lifts the parasites upwards in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil is a traditional male first name, so it serves as a man's given name.

clue.text: At home, I cut up mushrooms

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: to crop is to cut
someone at home is in
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook at home chops up some mushrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut up' reads as chopping, but it is a word for cut, turned upside down; that piece goes first even though it comes later in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcini are prized wild Italian fungi, also called ceps, so the plural noun matches the fungi named.

clue.text: First in team to request job

indicators.note: 'first in' points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: its opening letter
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: The first person in a team gets to ask for a particular job.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests team captains picking work.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work to be done, a straightforward synonym for an assigned piece of employment.

clue.text: A way to transfer funds blocked by university's old computer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something blocked has an obstruction sitting inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: BACS is the British automated bank payment system used for direct transfers
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A university's antiquated computer stops a payment going through.
explanation.walkthrough: BACS (Bankers' Automated Clearing Services) is the UK system for paying wages and bills directly between bank accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads on wires used for arithmetic was the earliest calculating device, humorously an ancient computer.

clue.text: Power likely open to manipulation

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
liable to happen means likely

explanation.surface: Power that can probably be abused or bent to someone's will.
explanation.walkthrough: P for power is standard; liable and likely overlap in 'liable to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pliable bends easily, and a pliable person is easily influenced, hence readily swayed by others.

clue.text: Tactical unit undercover ultimately within the law

indicators.note: within means inside, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: the cops are the police, informally the law

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: A squad of undercover agents is working inside the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The law' is slang for the police; 'undercover' sounds like part of the story but only lends its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A corps is a military formation of several divisions, or any organised body of troops in the field.

clue.text: One working, in charge of classic architecture

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective naming a classical style; the definition is a noun phrase

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a machine that is working is on
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A worker is put in charge of a project in the classical style.
explanation.walkthrough: Three short standard pieces; 'of' just joins them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the three Greek orders of columns, with scroll-shaped capitals, a style of ancient building.

clue.text: Announced market price for photo

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so we go by how the words sound

parts.note: to market is to sell, and a price is a fee

explanation.surface: A price for a picture has been made public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Market' looks like a noun but is a verb meaning sell.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfie is a picture people take of themselves, usually on a phone, a kind of snapshot.

clue.text: A veggie mistakenly eating starter of rabbit gets upset

indicators.note: to eat is to take inside, so one piece goes inside the other
done mistakenly means done wrongly, so the letters end up in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a starter is what comes first, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A vegetarian who accidentally eats a bit of rabbit is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Veggie' is British slang for a vegetarian; the joke is that eating rabbit would upset one.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve someone is to distress or wrong them, a formal synonym of the verb to upset.

clue.text: Earwigs may be responsible for this autumnal event failing to open

definitions.text: Earwigs may be responsible for this

indicators.note: failing to open means losing the beginning, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: in autumn, leaves are dropping from the trees

explanation.surface: Earwig insects may be blamed for something that happens to falling leaves in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: Earwigs look like the insects, but an earwig is also slang for someone who listens in on others.
explanation.definitionFit: An earwig, in the informal sense, is a nosy listener, so secretly overhearing conversations is what earwigs do.

clue.text: Break stringed instrument case in three

parts.note: a viola is a stringed instrument

indicators.note: a case is the outside shell, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a stringed instrument's case into three pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like the instrument case, but it means the outside letters of the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate a law or rule is to break it, so the verbs are synonyms when a promise or agreement is involved.

clue.text: Uneven, like a plot of land?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: resembling a small piece of ground

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading: a patch is a small plot of ground, so something like one is patch-y.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchy means inconsistent or irregular in quality, and the joke reading builds an adjective from a vegetable plot.

clue.text: Mention work about type of licence

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; it completes the phrase rather than naming the noun

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the preceding words are read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to mention
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone refers to a job involving some sort of permit.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are turned around together, so the work ends up first.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic licence is the freedom writers take to bend facts or grammar, so the word names that kind of permission.

clue.text: Track being regularly unavailable

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A railway or race track keeps being closed to use.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the odd letters: TrAcKbEiNg.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat or partner that is taken is already occupied or spoken for, so no longer free.

clue.text: River runs on high land mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the final letter is dropped
in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it, so this piece is placed second

parts.note: Tibet, the high plateau north of the Himalayas, without its final letter
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A river flows over a high plateau for most of its length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' sounds like a river flowing but is the letter R; 'on' puts it after the shortened land.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiber is the river that flows through Rome, so it is a proper name for a specific river.

clue.text: Height of Glaswegian church seat

parts.note: ben is the Scottish word for a mountain peak, as in Ben Nevis
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: How tall is the pew a person from Glasgow sits on in church?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Height' reads as a measurement but is a mountain, and Glaswegian signals the Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bench is a long seat for several people, like a pew in a church or a park bench.

clue.text: Long formula chemist pens

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the words hold the answer inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A chemist writes out a lengthy formula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the formula, but it is the verb meaning yearn; the answer straddles formulA CHEmist.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to yearn or pine for it, the same as longing for it.

clue.text: Soft rock from Wings in Cork covering Prince

indicators.note: to cover is to wrap around, so one piece goes around the other
wings are the two sides, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: its outer letters
Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: Soft rock music from the band Wings, played in the Irish city of Cork, covering a Prince song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft rock' and 'Wings' (Paul McCartney's band) suggest music; Prince is the singer too, but here it is Shakespeare's Prince Hal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chalk is a soft white limestone, the kind of crumbly stone that forms England's white cliffs.

clue.text: Improve small space with hazard, removing lead

indicators.note: the lead is the front, so removing it drops the first letter

parts.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em
chance, a risk or hazard, without its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone improves a cramped room by taking out a dangerous cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' suggests an electric cable, but it means the first letter. To hazard is to chance.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance something is to raise its quality or value, which is to make it better.

clue.text: Teen and I try changing age

indicators.note: changing means altering, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teenager and I try to change our ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Age' reads as how old someone is, but it is the long-period sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An age, informally, is a very long time, as in waiting for ages, which an eternity also is.

clue.text: Get lost, reportedly in Oxford?

indicators.note: reportedly means as said or heard, so we go by the sound of the word

parts.note: shoo is what you say to chase someone away

explanation.surface: Someone is told to clear off, as is said in Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford looks like the city, but it is a style of lace-up leather footwear; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a classic laced leather brogue-style footwear, so it is one example of the item.
